description.purpose: The container this assistant's channels are instantiated into. It ships empty and open: no cells, no ports, no contract of its own. Its whole job is to be an address that already exists, so the assistant can wire its reasoning core and its tool surface to ONE place instead of once per channel -- that is the point of GH #303, and it is why this container is part of the template rather than something an operator builds by hand.
description.use_when: Never on its own -- it travels with assistant@1.0.1. One channel is TWO nodes instantiated into this container, a connector and a talky, plus the edges that pair them: telegram-connector@2.0.0 is one cell and is addressed as that cell, talky@4.2.2 is a sealed hive and is addressed by path and lane. TRANSIT, derived from the occupants a channel is built from at this HEAD -- IN, carried down to the talky by the per-channel mutation: in_turn, in_bundle, in_advice, in_sweep, in_prune, in_round_sweep (the six the assistant carries in) plus in_tool (the tool surface's answer, re-stamped by the assistant's own edge). OUT, up to the assistant path: turn and error (normalised from the connector's ONE wire, told apart by hop.error_code), tool (the surface's call, which the assistant's guarded default carries to the tool surface unless it names a consult errand), and write, turn_write, extraction, recall, prune, error from the talky. answer never leaves: it is the connector's inbound edge, paired inside this container.
description.not_in_scope: No ports, because a sealed hive refuses exactly the endpoints a channel instantiation needs (hive_port_boundary) -- and the pairing edge between a connector and its talky is such an endpoint, below this hive's own path, which is the wiring this container exists for. No slot: GH #285's slot governs an address that does not exist, and this container does exist, so the declared unbound word could never fire -- see unbound_slot_behaviour in crates/meclaw-colony/src/colony.rs, which steps aside as soon as the target is a registered hive scope. No params.contract either, and here that is load-bearing rather than conventional: this container is wired by its own level the moment the assistant is instantiated, so mutation::hive_contract::check_lane_doors sees a WIRED hive from birth (hive_path_is_wired) and would then owe a door inside for every declared accepts lane. An empty container has no inside, so every declared lane would refuse EVERY later mutation of the colony until the first channel stands here -- and an assistant with no channel yet is a legitimate intermediate state. The transit list above is therefore prose the instantiating mutation reads, not a declaration the substrate enforces against an empty container; the lanes themselves are declared by the LEVEL, whose own edges satisfy the door and exit check from birth. No cells: what stands in this container is a channel, and a channel is instantiated, never shipped.
